title: Does QUF Imply QIND-CCA2 or QIND-CCA1?
summary: Conditioned on the existence of a QUF-but-not-QAE symmetric-key quantum encryption scheme, it remains open whether QUF implies QIND-CCA2, or QIND-CCA1 if the stronger implication fails.

formal_statement.body: Conditioned on the existence of a symmetric-key quantum encryption scheme satisfying quantum unforgeability (QUF) but not QAE, determine whether $\mathrm{QUF}\Rightarrow\mathrm{QIND\text{-}CCA2}$ (quantum indistinguishability under adaptive chosen-ciphertext attack); if that implication fails, determine whether $\mathrm{QUF}\Rightarrow\mathrm{QIND\text{-}CCA1}$.

scope.domain: Security relations for symmetric-key quantum encryption schemes.
assumptions: Existence of a symmetric-key quantum encryption scheme satisfying quantum unforgeability (QUF) but not QAE.
parameters: QUF and QAE, the security properties defining the premise
QIND-CCA2 and QIND-CCA1, the primary and fallback implication targets
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether QUF implies QIND-CCA2; if that implication fails, determine whether QUF implies QIND-CCA1.

progress.summary: The paper's discussion lists this among several open questions. After asking whether a QUF-but-not-QAE scheme exists, it asks whether QUF implies QIND-CCA2 or QIND-CCA1.
citation_labels: Gorjan Alagic et al., Unforgeable Quantum Encryption
